t.d: Venetian hot-worked glass, concentrated on Murano since 1291.
t.tech: hot-working; millefiori, murrine, sommerso, filigrana, calcedonio
t.auth: Artistic Glass Murano trademark (1994); Asian and Eastern European imitations are common

t.d: Cut, engraved and coloured glass from the Czech lands.
t.tech: wheel cutting and engraving, cased and coloured glass
t.auth: maker marks; early Bohemian crystal contained no lead

t.d: Moulded and frosted art glass in the manner of René Lalique.
t.tech: press-moulding, frosting, opalescent glass
t.auth: 'R. LALIQUE FRANCE' mark and model number

t.d: Art glass from the Småland glassworks, with Orrefors and Kosta as leading houses.
t.tech: Graal, Ariel, Ravenna and Kraka techniques; engraving
t.auth: engraved signature with technique and number

t.d: Dutch tin-glazed earthenware painted in cobalt blue.
t.tech: tin glaze over earthenware, painted in metal oxides
t.auth: factory marks and monograms from c. 1640; 'Delfts Blauw' mark on Royal Delft

t.d: Ottoman fritware painted under the glaze in cobalt, turquoise and bole red.
t.tech: underglaze painting on fritware with white slip
t.auth: style sequence: Abraham of Kütahya, Golden Horn, Damascus, Rhodian

t.d: The first European hard-paste porcelain.
t.tech: hard-paste porcelain, overglaze enamels, underglaze blue
t.auth: crossed swords mark (from 1720), variants help date pieces

t.p: Late Muromachi period (16th century) to present
t.d: Japanese art of appreciating incense by codified manners, one of the three classical arts of refinement.
t.tech: Agarwood slivers heated on a mica plate over ash in a censer; incense-guessing games
t.mat: Kyara and jinkō agarwood, sandalwood, aromatics
t.auth: Wood grade and origin of the agarwood; school-specific utensils such as the Shino incense packet

t.r: Arabian Peninsula, Gulf and wider Muslim world
t.d: Burning scented chips, pastilles and agarwood in a mabkhara to perfume homes and welcome guests.
t.tech: Indirect burning on charcoal in a censer
t.auth: Real agarwood is dense, dark and resinous; adulteration and plantation wood are common

t.d: Stickless herbal incense from monastery and Tibetan-medicine formulas.
t.tech: Extruded into lengths or coils, no bamboo core
t.mat: Himalayan herbs, often 30 or more ingredients
t.auth: Traceable lineage to a monastery or medical college; authentic Himalayan herbs

t.p: Ancient; bamboo-core stick from the late 19th century
t.d: Indian stick incense made from a paste on bamboo, scented with masala or perfume oils.
t.tech: Hand-rolled masala paste on bamboo; dhoop rolled or extruded without a core
t.mat: Charcoal or sawdust, jiggit binder, halmaddi resin, sandalwood
t.auth: Hand-rolled masala texture versus dipped charcoal sticks

t.r: Lauscha, Thuringia, Germany (and Neustadt bei Coburg, Bavaria)
t.d: Glassblowing town where moulded coloured glass ornaments and the glass bauble originated.
t.tech: Mouth- and mould-blown glass, silvered inside by hand and hand-painted
t.auth: Mouth-blown with hand-silvered interior; Inge-Glas pieces carry the Star Crown (from 1987).

t.d: Wooden toy and Christmas-figure making that replaced declining ore mining around Seiffen.
t.tech: lathe turning incl. Reifendrehen (ring turning), carving, painting
t.auth: Maker's stamp or label from an Ore Mountains workshop; hand-turned and hand-painted parts

t.d: Lathe-turned limbless dolls first sold by kijishi turners to hot-spring visitors, in regional styles tied to onsen.
t.tech: lathe turning, hand painting
t.auth: Traditional pieces follow the shape and painting of their onsen style

t.p: present centre Nusnäs; known abroad since 1939
t.d: Carved pine horses painted in the kurbits style, a symbol of Dalarna and Sweden.
t.tech: band-saw cutting, hand carving, kurbits painting
t.auth: Hand-painted kurbits so no two are identical; maker's label from a Nusnäs workshop

t.d: Nesting dolls turned in linden and painted in regional styles.
t.tech: lathe turning, painting
t.auth: Turned, not carved from one block; regional painting style

t.d: Mould-blown, silvered and hand-painted glass Christmas ornaments, exported worldwide from the 1840s.
t.tech: lamp-blowing into clay moulds, silver-nitrate silvering, hand painting
t.auth: Blown in Lauscha by one of the small family glass-blowing firms (about 20 in 2009)

t.d: Festival dolls in Heian court dress displayed on tiers for Hinamatsuri.
t.tech: carved and dressed doll making, from folded paper to carved figures
t.auth: Arrangement follows Kantō or Kansai convention; court dress follows Heian style

t.d: Papier-mâché daruma made from the charm moulds of Shōrinzan Daruma-ji.
t.tech: papier-mâché over moulds, weighted base, painting
t.auth: Takasaki-made, sold with blank eyes

t.d: Making decorated sweet-filled piñatas for Las Posadas and birthdays, a Mexican tradition traced to Acolman.
t.tech: clay pot or cardboard/papier-mâché shell, often over a balloon, covered in crepe paper
ctr: San Juan de la Puerta, Guanajuato
t.auth: hand-made shell and crepe-paper cones; traditional star form with seven points

t.d: China's main centre of firework and firecracker making for over 1,400 years, exporting since 1875.
t.tech: hand and factory filling of paper-cased crackers and shells
t.auth: Liuyang fireworks are a protected origin product

t.d: Industrial yet hand-painted terracotta gnome making that made Gräfenroda the centre of the garden gnome.
t.tech: clay slip poured into moulds, kiln-fired and hand-painted
t.auth: Fired, hand-painted terracotta from a Gräfenroda manufactory, not plaster, resin or plastic copies.

t.d: Mouth-blown glass summer wind bells from Tokyo, painted from the inside.
t.tech: glass blown without a mould; rim ground jagged for the ring; inside painting
t.mat: glass, oil- and water-based paints, paper strip
t.auth: uneven ground rim, painting on the inside, traditional vermilion-and-green strip

t.d: Cast-iron ware of the old Nanbu domain, known for tea kettles and iron wind bells.
t.tech: hand iron casting; some pieces finished with Joboji urushi
t.auth: made in Morioka or Oshu by recognised workshops
